comment: A Clean definition module is declarations only, so its declared interface IS the file. Pins all four `signature_name` shapes (identifier, constructor-as-function, parenthesized_operator, parenthesized_name) each publishing a symbol marked as a declaration AND appearing in the export list. Measured pre-fix: a `.dcl` yielded its module symbol and nothing else, and the export predicate `!sym.ownerName` — the exact negation of the rule its own comment stated — left 312 of 312 corpus files exporting at most one thing. Mutant `clean/declarations-not-published` reverts exactly this state.

expectSymbols.name: NSMakeSize
expectSymbols.comment: uppercase name typed `constructor` by the grammar: Clean lets an uppercase name be a FUNCTION
`(%.` infixl 9 :: …` — the published name is the unparenthesized operator

expectSymbols.name: bitxor
expectSymbols.comment: `(bitxor) :: …` — a parenthesized NAME, not an operator symbol

expectExportsNote: expectExports matches fields EXACTLY, so no `comment` key may appear inside an entry. The export list is the module's interface: a declared name that does not appear here is not importable.

forbidSymbols.comment: a parenthesized shape must never leak its punctuation as a name
an operator declaration is a function, never a type

expectRelationships.comment: each declaration's membership edge carries THAT declaration's line (M59.O2) — the four shapes are on four consecutive lines, so a per-set or off-by-one line cannot pass all four
